title: Investigating Trojan Attacks on Pre-trained Language Model-powered Database Middleware

problem.claim: Malicious pre-trained language models may pose security threats to database middleware that relies on them.

gap.claim: The security risks of untrusted third-party pre-trained language models in database middleware have not been fully explored.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a Trojan attack in which a maliciously designed pre-trained language model causes unexpected behavior in database middleware.
The proposed Trojan attacks are characterized by triggerability, imperceptibility, and generalizability across downstream tasks.
The paper evaluates the impact of the Trojan attacks and analyzes potential countermeasures and their limitations.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper explicitly proposes a novel type of Trojan attack against pre-trained language model-powered database middleware.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report thoroughly evaluating the impact of the Trojan attacks through experiments.
The authors report analyzing potential countermeasures and their limitations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Pre-trained language models have enabled database middleware such as natural language query interfaces and entity matching.
The use of untrusted third-party pre-trained language models creates insufficiently explored security risks.
The paper proposes a Trojan attack that causes unexpected behavior in database middleware.
The attack operates normally on ordinary inputs, requires no noticeable input modification, and can target multiple downstream tasks.
The authors report experiments, countermeasure analysis, and possible implications for stronger PLM implementation mechanisms.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the experimental datasets, metrics, attack implementation, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not identify the proposed countermeasures or detail their limitations.
The abstract does not provide a concrete implementation mechanism for stronger PLM deployment.
